A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same targeted augmentation study and contain readable text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–F. The retained method, theory, and experiments can be reliably matched across renaming, renumbering, and added material.

before.justification: v2 reports original classification and transfer-learning experiments on CIFAR10/100, TinyImageNet, Flowers-102, Aircraft, and Stanford Cars, together with ablations in Section 5 and Appendix F.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds ImageNet classification, MS-COCO detection, and further CIFAR10 analyses in Appendix F.

M1.justification: The classification algorithm and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged apart from TADA naming. Appendix F.4 adds a detection-specific adaptation: selecting images containing at least one misclassified object and using released instance-inpainted synthetic images, instead of the classification implementation’s classwise clustering.

E1.justification: v3 adds direct training and evaluation on full ImageNet and MS-COCO object detection (Appendices F.3–F.4). v2 used ImageNet-pretrained models for downstream classification but reported neither experiment. These additions substantially broaden dataset coverage and introduce object localization beyond image classification.

E2.justification: v3 adds evaluated comparisons with Boomerang on ImageNet and InstanceAugmentation on COCO (Tables 9–10), plus targeted versus full-data TrivialAugment controls in Table 5. UPSAMPLE is retained under the name USEFUL; it is not a newly added baseline.

E3.justification: New protocols include 16-epoch ImageNet training of ResNet18/50, selection at epoch 2, and 65% augmentation; COCO uses YOLOv5m, 300 epochs, batch size 40, epoch-5 selection, and AP50/mAP50–95 evaluation. Table 5 applies TrivialAugment only to augmented copies, distinct from the retained online augmentation experiment. Existing classification settings remain.

E4.justification: v3 adds controls testing targeted selection with non-diffusion augmentation (Table 5), sensitivity to two through four clusters and the augmented fraction (Figure 10), and training-loss comparisons with upsampling (Figure 9). These address selection specificity, clustering sensitivity, and optimization beyond the retained denoising, amplification-factor, and gradient-variance analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions already report error bars and values with ± uncertainty. v3 newly specifies that Figure 10’s error bars are standard deviations across runs. Neither version supplies run counts or seeds; the additional uncertainty-bearing result rows do not establish an increase in repetitions.

E6.justification: Retained tables preserve their scores, while v3 adds substantial results. Table 9 reports ResNet50 ImageNet top-1 accuracy of 74.77% for TADA+Boomerang versus 73.72% for Boomerang. Table 10 reports COCO mAP50–95 of 46.28 versus 45.75 for TADA+InstanceAugmentation and InstanceAugmentation. Table 5 adds targeted-TA versus full-TA errors of 4.26% versus 4.48%; Figures 9–10 add loss and clustering findings. These are new comparisons, not same-setting improvements over v2.

T1.justification: Definitions 3.1–3.2, Theorems 4.1–4.3, Corollary 4.4, and the assumptions, derivations, and proofs in Appendices A–D are retained. The added descriptions of standard detection metrics introduce no new mathematical result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion extend the claimed contribution to ImageNet scalability and effectiveness beyond classification through object detection. The central selective-augmentation, homogeneous-learning, and SGD-versus-SAM claims remain, but the headline applicability scope substantially expands.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the targeted-TrivialAugment control as isolating selection benefits beyond diffusion and interprets the new benchmarks as supporting scalability and dense prediction. Appendix F.3 also acknowledges computational constraints behind the short ImageNet training budget. Existing explanations concerning noise overfitting, FID tradeoffs, and gradient variance remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds a TADA code-access link and documents the FFCV implementation, Stable Diffusion v1.5/Boomerang generation, selection checkpoints, YOLOv5m training settings, and the released detection augmentation source. Existing classification hyperparameters, hardware, and generation-time disclosures remain; removing the duplicated main-text training paragraph does not remove those details from Appendix F.1.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands discussion of GenMix, Diff-Mix, Diff-II, SaSPA, DiffCoRe-Mix, and Boomerang. It qualifies the earlier emphasis on expensive 10–30× augmentation by acknowledging methods using 1× augmentation and positions targeted selection as complementary to generation pipelines. References supporting the new experiments are added, while Dunlap et al. (2023) is removed.

P1.justification: v3 edits the abstract, introduction, conclusion, and related-work prose, introduces TADA and USEFUL terminology, updates author/header information, and adds acknowledgements. Training details are consolidated in Appendix F.1 and new experimental subsections are appended. The overall section order and most method and theory prose remain stable.

P2.justification: The visual evidence expands with ImageNet accuracy plots, training-loss and cluster-sensitivity plots (Figures 3, 9–10), and targeted-TA, ImageNet, and COCO tables (Tables 5, 9–10). Existing displays are largely retained with updated legends, renumbering, and reflow; the first-page author block is also condensed.

improvement.justification: The ImageNet comparisons directly test the central selection argument at substantially larger scale, while the targeted-TA and cluster controls examine design assumptions left untested in v2. COCO adds evidence of transfer beyond classification. Together these substantially strengthen empirical support for selective augmentation. The gains outweigh remaining reporting weaknesses: ImageNet is tested only for 16 epochs, run counts remain unspecified, and the headline 30–40% augmentation wording does not adequately reflect the 65% ImageNet and 75% COCO settings.
